title: gridwatch exec plugin protocol (§4.7, D32/D39, arc 8b) — one JSON object per line, both directions
description: Every line a plugin writes is validated against this before the host looks at it. A line that does not validate is a protocol error, and three of them stop the plugin rather than restarting it. The host's own lines are validated in tests, so a plugin author can rely on their shape.

hello.description: host → plugin, once, first. `contract` is the compatibility promise.

capabilities.description: What this machine can do, by the host's names (Procfs, Nvml, …). A plugin should degrade rather than fail when one it wants is missing.

keys.description: Metric names already in the host's catalogue, so a plugin does not invent a colliding one.

manifest.description: plugin → host, once, in answer to hello. Validated against manifest.schema.json as well.

sample.description: plugin → host, any time: one metric reading. A source plugin's whole job.

key.description: `<source>.<metric>`, lower case. The host prefixes it with the plugin's own id, so a plugin cannot publish over a built-in key.

label.description: A name or an index; null (or absent) for an unlabelled key.

at.description: Nanoseconds since the epoch. Absent means 'now' by the host's clock, which is what a plugin should send unless it is replaying.

render.description: host → plugin: draw this instance at this size. Sent only when a visible tile's inputs changed.

view.description: plugin → host: the view tree for a render. No cells and no colours — the host's renderer draws it through the theme, which is why a plugin cannot break the look of the dashboard.

key.description: host → plugin: a keystroke, while the tile is captured.
A single character, or a name: up down left right enter esc tab backspace home end pgup pgdn f1..f12.

command.description: plugin → host: a side effect. Deliberately a small set — a plugin may ask for a toast or a page, and may not signal a process, write a file or run a program.

status.description: plugin → host: health, like a source's. `unavailable` with a reason is how a plugin says it cannot work here — it is not an error and does not count as a strike.

log.description: plugin → host: a line for the log file, never the screen. A plugin's stderr goes to the same place.
